cues.text: Knowing the fabric helps us clean it the right way. First, natural fabrics. They come from plants and animals.
Cotton comes from a plant. It is soft and strong. Most dress shirts are cotton. It can shrink in hot water.
Linen comes from the flax plant. It feels cool and crisp, and it wrinkles very easily. Look for little bumps in the threads.
Wool comes from sheep. Suits, coats, and sweaters are often wool. Hot water and rubbing make it shrink, so we dry clean it.
Silk is shiny, smooth, and light. Water can leave spots and make the color run, so we dry clean it.
Cashmere comes from goats. It is super soft and expensive. It gets little fuzz balls, so handle it gently.
At the counter, read the label and feel the fabric.
For wool, silk, cashmere, and linen, choose the fabric on the ticket. These can have a small extra charge.
If you are not sure what it is, ask a manager.
